answers.content: Create a new REST API. Add a resource that has a single GET method that is integrated with the updated version of the Lambda function.
answers.explanation: Creating a new REST API doubles API management effort and is unnecessary given stage variable functionality.

answers.content: Update the Lambda integration of the existing GET method to point to the updated version of the Lambda function. Deploy the new version.
answers.explanation: Updating the integration directly affects production and does not allow isolated testing before promotion.

questions.content:
A company runs continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for
its application on AWS CodePipeline. A developer must write unit tests and run
them as part of the pipelines before staging the artifacts for testing.

How should the developer incorporate unit tests as part of CI/CD pipelines?

answers.content: Create a separate CodePipeline pipeline to run unit tests.
answers.explanation: Creating a separate pipeline to run unit tests adds unnecessary complexity and is not the standard practice for integrating tests within CI/CD pipelines.

answers.content: Update the AWS CodeBuild build specification to include a phase for running unit tests.
answers.explanation: AWS CodeBuild build specifications are designed to run build phases including unit tests within the CI/CD pipeline. Unit tests should be incorporated into the build process to verify application code before progressing to later pipeline stages. Running unit tests as part of the CodeBuild phase aligns with AWS best practices of automated testing integrated into the build lifecycle.

answers.content: Install the AWS CodeDeploy agent on an Amazon EC2 instance to run unit tests.
answers.explanation: Installing CodeDeploy agent on EC2 for unit tests is not appropriate, as CodeDeploy is for deployment, not running unit tests in the build phase.

answers.content: Create a testing branch in a git repository for the pipelines to run unit tests.
answers.explanation: Creating a testing branch does not directly integrate unit test execution into the pipeline; branching alone does not run tests.

questions.content:
A developer is troubleshooting a three-tier application, which is deployed on
Amazon EC2 instances. There is a connectivity problem between the application
servers and the database servers.

Which AWS services or tools should be used to identity the faulty component?
(Choose two.)

answers.content: AWS CloudTrail
answers.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs API calls but does not capture network traffic or connectivity issues directly between servers.

answers.content: AWS Trusted Advisor
answers.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor provides best practice checks but is not designed for real-time troubleshooting of network connectivity.

answers.content: Amazon VPC Flow Logs
Network access control lists
E. AWS Config rules
answers.explanation: AWS Config rules assess configuration compliance but do not provide detailed network traffic data needed for connectivity troubleshooting.

questions.content:
A developer is making changes to a custom application that uses AWS Elastic
Beanstalk.

Which solutions will update the Elastic Beanstalk environment with the new
application version after the developer completes the changes? (Choose two.)

answers.content: Package the application code into a zip file. Use the AWS Management Console to upload the .zip file and deploy the packaged application.
Package the application code into a .tar file. Use the AWS Management Console to create a new application version from the .tar file. Update the environment by using the AWS CLI.
answers.explanation: Packaging as .tar and using the AWS CLI is not supported based on the tutorial’s focus and standard Elastic Beanstalk usage.

answers.content: Package the application code into a .tar file. Use the AWS Management Console to upload the .tar file and deploy the packaged application.
answers.explanation: Uploading a .tar file via the AWS Management Console is not supported or mentioned in the supplied facts.

answers.content: Package the application code into a .zip file. Use the AWS CL to create a new application version from the .zip file and to update the environment.
E. Package the application code into a .zip file. Use the AWS Management Console to create a new application version from the .zip file. Rebuild the environment by using the AWS CLI.
answers.explanation: Rebuilding the environment is unnecessary to deploy a new application version; updating the environment is sufficient.

questions.content:
A developer needs to write an AWS CloudFormation template on a local machine and
deploy a CloudFormation stack to AWS.

What must the developer do to complete these tasks?

answers.content: Install the AWS CLI. Configure the AWS CLI by using an IAM user name and password.
answers.explanation: IAM user username and password cannot be used to configure AWS CLI for programmatic access.

answers.content: Install the AWS CLI. Configure the AWS CLI by using an SSH key.
answers.explanation: SSH keys are not applicable for AWS CLI authentication.

answers.content: Install the AWS CLI, Configure the AWS CLI by using an IAM user access key and secret key.
answers.explanation: AWS CLI is required to interact with AWS services including CloudFormation locally. AWS CLI authentication requires an IAM access key and secret key, not username/password or SSH keys. Using IAM user access keys aligns with AWS best practices for CLI access and automation. IAM user name and password or SSH keys are not valid methods for AWS CLI configuration. X.509 certificates via SDK are not the typical or recommended method for CloudFormation deployment in this scenario.

answers.content: Install an AWS software development kit (SDK). Configure the SDK by using an X.509 certificate.
answers.explanation: Using an SDK with X.509 certificates is not standard practice for CLI-based CloudFormation deployment.

questions.content:
A large company has its application components distributed across multiple AWS
accounts. The company needs to collect and visualize trace data across these
accounts.

What should be used to meet these requirements?

answers.content: AWS X-Ray
answers.explanation: AWS X-Ray is designed specifically for collecting and visualizing trace data, including across multiple AWS accounts. It provides a managed service for tracing application components and analyzing performance issues and errors. Other options do not provide direct support for trace data collection and visualization across accounts.

answers.content: Amazon CloudWatch
answers.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch collects metrics and logs but is not primarily used for trace data visualization across accounts.

answers.content: Amazon VPC flow logs
answers.explanation: Amazon VPC flow logs capture network traffic data, not application trace data.

answers.content: Amazon OpenSearch Service
answers.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service is for search and analytics but does not specifically handle distributed trace collection.

questions.content:
A developer must cache dependent artifacts from Maven Central, a public package
repository, as part of an application's build pipeline. The build pipeline has
an AWS CodeArtifact repository where artifacts of the build are published. The
developer needs a solution that requires minimum changes to the build pipeline.

Which solution meets these requirements?

answers.content: Modify the existing CodeAriifact repository to associate an upstream repository with the public package repository.
answers.explanation: Associating an upstream repository with the existing CodeArtifact repository allows caching artifacts from Maven Central with minimum changes to the build pipeline. This approach leverages managed CodeArtifact features designed to integrate public package repositories as upstream sources. It avoids the need to create new domains or repositories, thus maintaining minimal disruption. Modifying the existing repository is simpler and aligns with best practices of using managed AWS services and secure access.

answers.content: Create a new CodeAtfact repository that has an external connection to the public package repository.
answers.explanation: Creating a new repository introduces unnecessary complexity when the existing repository can be modified.

answers.content: Create a new CodeAifact domain that contains a new repository that has an external connection to the public package repository.
answers.explanation: Creating a new domain adds overhead and is not needed for upstream integration.

answers.content: Modify the CodeAnifact repository resource policy to allow artifacts to be fetched from the public package repository.
answers.explanation: Resource policies control access permissions and do not enable artifact fetching from public repositories.
